prompt:
Write a police officer's crash report narrative (about 150 words). Collision type: sideswipe while changing lanes in Baytown, Texas. The claimant was a driver and reported whiplash. Refer to people as Driver 1, Driver 2 or Passenger. No names, no dates. (Internal reference C-1276; do not mention it.) Work these facts into the text naturally, in your own words, without listing them:
- The reported injury is plausible for a crash like this one.
- Witnesses, photos and the other driver all confirm the accident happened as described.
- The vehicle damage matches the described impact.
- It is not fully clear where in the vehicle the claimant was sitting.
- No earlier damage to the vehicle is known.
- The driver is named on the policy.
text: Driver 1 was traveling in the right lane of the roadway in Baytown, Texas, when the vehicle began to drift into the adjacent lane as Driver 2 attempted a lane change. The two vehicles made contact along their sides, producing a sideswipe collision. Driver 1 reported neck pain consistent with whiplash following the impact. Witness statements, scene photographs, and Driver 2's account all align with the sequence of events as described by Driver 1, and the damage visible on both vehicles corresponds to the angle and force of a sideswipe. Responding officers found no indication of prior damage to either vehicle in the areas affected. Driver 1 is listed as the named insured on the policy involved. Officers were unable to confirm with certainty whether a Passenger was present in the vehicle at the time of impact, and the seating position of Driver 1 at the moment of the collision remains unclear from the information gathered at the scene. The injury complaint appears reasonable given the nature of the collision, and the vehicle was towed from the scene for further inspection.
